rebuttal_or_critique: I maintain my firm stance. While headline inflation has moderated to 4.25%, the core inflation print of 5.02% remains uncomfortably high, signaling that underlying price pressures are persistent. With the economy operating at a positive output gap of 0.50% and GVA growth robust at 7.80%, the economy is demonstrating resilience that does not necessitate a premature pivot to a neutral stance. The 'withdrawal of accommodation' is a vital signal of our commitment to price stability; shifting now, while core inflation remains significantly above our 4.00% target, would risk unanchoring inflation expectations. We must remain vigilant against potential food price shocks and external spillovers from the US Fed's policy trajectory. I cannot support a shift to neutral until we see more durable evidence of core inflation aligning with our target.
